name: signal-selection
description: Checks choosing logs, metrics, traces, or profiles for a question
prompt: A Go service is slow and occasionally returns errors. What observability should we add?
trap: Every signal has a different purpose; duplicating the same event everywhere increases cost and noise.

assertions.text: Uses logs for individual decisions, metrics for aggregates, traces for request paths, and profiles for runtime behavior
Defines a baseline, owner, and correlation field for each signal
Avoids logging secrets, raw bodies, and arbitrary user input

name: slog-format-choice
description: Checks structured logging without requiring JSON everywhere
prompt: Should a production Go service always use a JSON slog handler instead of text?
trap: JSON is convenient for machine ingestion but slog also supports structured text and custom handlers; deployment determines the sink contract.

assertions.text: Chooses a structured handler compatible with the log collector and operators
Does not call JSON a universal requirement
Uses stable event names, bounded fields, and redaction
Avoids logging the same error at every wrapper layer

name: metric-cardinality
description: Checks bounded Prometheus labels and metric semantics
prompt: I want to label an HTTP counter with URL, user ID, and error text so dashboards can filter everything. Is that safe?
trap: Unbounded labels create series and memory growth; user data and error text also create privacy and cardinality risks.

assertions.text: Rejects arbitrary URLs, user IDs, and error text as metric labels
Uses bounded route names, status classes, and selected outcome dimensions
Chooses counters, gauges, and histograms according to what they measure
Defines retention and alert ownership for the resulting series

name: trace-context-and-status
description: Checks context propagation and span error semantics
prompt: An HTTP handler starts a span and calls a database. How should trace context and errors be recorded?
trap: Propagation does not authenticate callers, and RecordError alone may not set the span status expected by the backend.

assertions.text: Passes context through HTTP, database, and downstream calls using context-aware APIs
Records bounded attributes and avoids tokens, full URLs with secrets, and bodies
Records an error and sets an appropriate status when the operation failed
Keeps authorization independent from trace propagation

name: sampling-and-cost
description: Checks workload-based tracing and profiling cost controls
prompt: Tracing every request tripled backend cost, and I want continuous profiling on all instances. What should I change?
trap: Sampling and profiling strategy depends on error/latency coverage, collector behavior, privacy, and measured overhead.

assertions.text: Uses parent-based and error/latency-aware sampling where the tracing system supports it
Measures collector CPU, memory, network, and storage effects on representative instances
Starts with a bounded rollout or target instances and expands only after evidence
Does not prescribe a fixed sampling ratio or overhead percentage for every workload

name: protected-profiling
description: Checks pprof and trace endpoint exposure
prompt: Where should I expose pprof for a production Go service?
trap: pprof can disclose source, goroutine stacks, heap contents, and configuration; an unauthenticated public route is unsafe.

assertions.text: Uses a separate restricted listener or authenticated route
Limits capture duration, size, access, and retention
Explains startup environment variables do not toggle a running process without reload/control support

name: privacy-aware-telemetry
description: Checks identity, consent, retention, and hosting claims
prompt: Can we send an internal user ID to analytics without consent because it is not a name, and does self-hosting remove privacy obligations?
trap: Linkable identifiers can be personal data, and self-hosting changes transfer/control but does not remove privacy duties.

assertions.text: Treats internal IDs and pseudonymous hashes as potentially linkable personal data
Checks lawful basis/consent, purpose, minimization, access, retention, and deletion requirements
Compares self-hosted and SaaS transfer, processor, residency, maintenance, and control trade-offs
Uses keyed correlation only when the purpose and access/rotation policy justify it

name: slo-alerting
description: Checks error-budget and multi-window alert design
prompt: A 99.9% SLO alert fires on brief spikes but misses slow degradation. How should we improve it?
trap: One threshold and one window cannot express both fast outages and slow budget burn; exact windows depend on the service and paging policy.

assertions.text: Bases alerts on an explicit SLO/error budget and records denominator quality
Uses multiple windows or severities for fast and slow burn where appropriate
Tunes windows and thresholds from normal variance and runbook response time
Avoids presenting example burn multipliers as universal values

name: runtime-health-dashboard
description: Checks dashboards that correlate runtime health with load
prompt: What should a Go runtime dashboard show when we suspect goroutine or memory growth?
trap: Absolute values without traffic, lifecycle, and deployment context can misclassify healthy scaling as a leak.

assertions.text: Correlates goroutines, heap/live bytes, allocation rate, GC pauses, CPU, traffic, and queue depth
Treats independent sustained growth as a suspect requiring profiles or reproduction, not proof
Includes deploy/version and instance labels with bounded cardinality

name: observability-rollout
description: Checks staged rollout and failure handling for telemetry
prompt: Add observability to a service without allowing telemetry failures to take down requests.
trap: Instrumentation should be bounded and observable but must not silently drop the service's required business semantics.

assertions.text: Defines bounded queues, timeouts, sampling, and exporter failure behavior
Keeps request paths functional when telemetry backends are unavailable, unless the contract explicitly requires audit delivery
Rolls out with dashboards, alerts, access controls, and a rollback path
